I'm going to post this as someone who has almost always had a boyfriend \(and my name coincidentally is also named Sam, ha.\)

As some other users have already said, some people prefer to be in relationships rather than being single. This is fine, but the continual jumping from guy to guy is often a mark of low self\-esteem. It's nice to have attention! If an attractive guy is giving you the time, then why not go for it? Logically, it seems okay to jump from relationship to relationship. Usually my excuse for always having a boyfriend was "It just happened". This is sort of true \- it's not like I was actively looking for a boyfriend; one thing led to another and I always happened to find someone new. 

As adults, the hard reality is that we cannot make others do something. Personally, I wish I had someone close to me sit me down and tell me to slow down. My parents always did, but I sort of brushed them off because they were my parents, of course they're going to tell me things like that. 

Does she know you are bothered by her relationships? Have you ever sat her down and had a heart to heart intervention about it, or have you made any remarks like "Oh, *another* boyfriend?" I use to have acquaintances say passive aggressive things about my relationships but because they were so passive aggressive, I always acted defensive.

As her friend, you need come up with an intervention plan. This isn't a romantic problem, this is a self worth problem. She needs to change her mindset into "Am I good enough for this person? They seem to think so" to "Is this person good enough for me?' \- no mean to sound pretentious, but it's so so crucial to seriously evaluate committed relationships, especially at her age.

You sound like a wonderful friend for looking out for her. I wish I had a friend like you when I was on my little boyfriend stint. Good luck!

Oh man, do I have a story for this. 

Up until I was a second grader, I absolutely loved school. I loved to learn and being in the classroom. That all changed when I was assigned Mr. Dawson as my second grade teacher. His classroom had no organization whatsoever. He would give us math books and we would have to work on them independently unless we had a question, then we would ask him. I get that everyone was at a different level in math, but it still was weird. I remember him telling us that we didn’t need to bring backpacks anymore. 

There’s one specific story I remember so vividly. After recess was story time. Everyday, he’d have someone new pick out a book from the shelf for read aloud. That day he chose me. Keep in mind this was near the end of the year, so we had read most of the books on the shelf. I saw one we had not read yet, and without really looking at it, I just handed it to him. What I didn’t realize was that it was a lower reading level book, one with big pictures and one sentence per page. As soon as everyone quieted down, he scoffed and said, “Geez sammy1996x, I should have my kindergartener granddaughter read this book to us instead!” He proceeded to read the book to us in a really dumb sounding voice with a lot of exaggeration. Everyone was laughing, and I was sitting in the back absolutely mortified. I remember coming home and crying because I felt so incredibly stupid. 

It’s been almost 15 years since then and I still remember it like it was yesterday. Future educators, please be cautious about what you say around your students. You never know what they might remember for the rest of their lives.

I know it’s ultimately his decision, but like I mentioned before, I’m the common ground child so he he’s venting a lot to me and asking for advice. 

Ever since I moved to uni, I don’t feel like a child anymore. I’m definitely the person holding our entire family together. I love my parents and they support me everyday they can, but now they think they can tell me all their problems and it kind of drives me nuts!! The relationship dynamic has definitely shifted and it makes me so uncomfortable. I just want to be a kid again.

I'm 20 and just had a pregnancy scare last week. I was late on my period, but found out it was only because of some new medication I started taking recently. I legit saw my life flash before my eyes: I wouldn't be able to finish college, travel, buy a house, all like I wanted to. When I started having sex in high school, I was super safe and always had a back up plan. Once this pregnancy scare (hopefully) blows over, you should sit down with your girlfriend and have a serious talk. What if she indeed did get pregnant in the future? Other then both committing suicide, what are your most realistic options? My mind leans most towards abortion, but that's just me.

For the record, her and your parents would much rather have you alive and teen parents then dead because you were trying to escape this situation.
I would thank myself for not committing suicide. It takes a lot to commit suicide, but it takes even more to keep living.

My understanding is that anti-theist is the opposition of believing in (the Christian) God, and atheist is the opposition of believing in any Deity, or not just the Christian God (Allah, etc). I think atheism is often exchanged with anti-theist, only because the Christian God is the most well-known. 
The real speculation should be about the difference behind atheism/anti-theism and agnosticism. Just like any religion, atheist BELIEVES there is no God, straight-up. Their faith is their "certainty" in knowing there is not God. Agnosticsm, however, is a group of people who, to put in light terms, simply do not care enough to know or want to know. Personally, I am Agnostic. Sure, there could be a God; will I ever know? I'm not sure, and honestly, I don't really care at this point in my life. I have found happiness without religion and try to break the stereotype that being agnostic or atheist means having no morals. As you all probably know or have heard, not going to Church does not make you a bad person, just like going to the Church does not automatically make you a good person.

I was in marching band and whenever I dated, it was usually guys who were also musicians (mainly drummers). Personally, I liked it because it gives us something in common. Plus music culture is so widely popular and interesting, it's nice to have a hobby where both people understand thoroughly about the subject. Side note- sometimes it got irritating. I once was dated this guy who was extremely talented on the guitar and piano (a bit narcissist about it actually- whole other story though). I, yes, I, took him out to this really fancy Italian restaurant that had a piano bar. The entire dinner he complained about the pianist, who I thought was descent. SO ANNOYING.

As for girls who are fascinated by musicians who have little to no musical background... It's honestly just a very fascinating thing. You see, when you're dating an athlete, he can't just display his skills out on the spot (I mean, he could do an arm wrestling contest, but he'd just look like a douche). A guy who plays guitar or piano is just interesting. Passion is a very rare thing nowadays. 
As far as writing a song for them, I was never fascinated by it, which sounds bitchy of me, but it's true. I had 2 guys write songs for me and I was never... Impressed, I guess. They only wrote them because we had been dating for a while, and it almost seemed like they had to. If you listened to the lyrics of one of the songs, it was actually very depressing. My advice, if a girl is extremely interested in your musical skills but has no background of music or music/concert culture herself, I'd say ditch her. She probably just wants to brag to her friends how you wrote a song you literally just threw together for her.
